newsitem.title: FRANCE: Crude bomb injures six in French city of Lyon.
newsitem.headline: Crude bomb injures six in French city of Lyon.

text.p: Six people were slightly injured on Tuesday when a crude bomb exploded outside a subsidiary of state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais in the central French city of Lyon, police said.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast, caused by a device made out of a tin can packed with nails.
"It was probably not a terrorist act," police sources said. They said they suspected a disgruntled client may have been responsible.
The bomb, which was set near an outside air vent, shattered several windows and caused other minor damage to the exterior of the building, a branch of consumer credit agency Finalion.
The six wounded people, suffering from slight shock, were sent to hospital for tests.
Corsican separatists have carried out a number bombings in mainland France since a much-breached truce expired last month.

Algerian-linked Moslem fundamentalists carried out a wave of bombings in Paris and the Lyon area last year, but investigators believe most of those involved are either in custody awaiting trial, abroad or dead.
